occurrences.key: [Should-fix] src/store/apply.rs:985
occurrences.text:
[Should-fix] src/store/apply.rs:985 — On a node with more than one non-named host kind, a parked unnamed own `seat.created` keeps PARKED_READY true while its materializer keeps re-parking it, so `apply_pass` spends every pass re-attempting it, never reaches log heads, and reports `has_more` forever. [lanes: data-migrations]
  verdict: confirmed (reproduce ✓ / refute ✗-survived / ground ✓)
  evidence: PARKED_READY narrowed by the diff to `kind<>'named'` (apply.rs:985) while `restore_own_seat` (src/store/seats/publication.rs ~286-310) now returns HostUnavailable when `count(DISTINCT kind)<=1` fails; facts/seat.rs:62-69 maps that to `Wait{on:Host}`; `reattempt_parked` (apply.rs:1005-1017) loops `next_reattemptable`, which ignores `run.attempted`, until `run.exhausted()`, then returns true so `apply_pass` breaks before `next_ready_head`; workers.rs:1386 re-hints on `has_more` with no backoff. Not executed; chain read from source by all three seats.
  fix-shape hint: make PARKED_READY mirror the materializer's single-kind condition (or have `next_reattemptable` skip rows in `run.attempted`), plus the spike test the finding names (two-kind store, own unnamed seat.created, two passes, second `has_more=false`).

[Should-fix] src/store/seats/publication.rs:245 — Own-log restore after a wipe brings a retired named seat back as a live `unresolved` seat holding the name, so the retired seat takes the name, its live successor is held nameless, and the next resolve of the name reattaches the retired seat. [lanes: data-migrations]
  verdict: confirmed (reproduce ✓ / refute ✗-survived / ground ✓)
  evidence: `restore_own_seat` (publication.rs ~239-290) inserts every own `seat.created` as `state='unresolved'` and never looks for a later `seat.retired`; `materialize_seat_retired` begins `if m.local_origin { return Ok(()); }`; `named_seat_apply` (resolution.rs ~740-760) selects `name=?2 AND state<>'retired'` and calls `reattach_named_seat` on an unresolved row. Design lines 418-419 say "Retire ends continuity for good". tests/store/named_restore.rs has no retired-before-restore case (its `retired` assertions at 309/338 follow a retire made after the restore).
  fix-shape hint: during own-log replay, let a local-origin `seat.retired` retire the restored row (or have restore skip a `seat.created` with a later own `seat.retired`), and add the A-created/A-retired/B-created replay test.

occurrences.key: [Should-fix] src/host/hc/mod.rs:877; src/host/hc/mod.rs:878
occurrences.text:
[Should-fix] src/host/hc/mod.rs:877; src/host/hc/mod.rs:878 — HcHost::enumerate_targets turns a failed core capture (socket gone, refused, decode error) into Ok with complete:false instead of Err, so observation takes the durable-invalidation path that ends every open binding on the core, while Health reports a causeless PartialEnumeration and reachability is marked up. [lanes: premortem, observability]
  verdict: confirmed (reproduce ✓ / refute ✗-survived / ground ✓)
  evidence: mod.rs:877-878 `let Some(capture) = self.capture() else { return Ok(Self::unverified(..)) }`; `capture()` (~328) collapses every failure via `.ok()?`; `unverified()` sets `complete:false`. reconcile.rs `observe_and_publish`: `Err(_)` → HostUnavailable (Frozen) but `!complete` → PartialEnumeration; `is_unavailability` (ports.rs:971) excludes it; hc is Closing so `invalidate_host_observation` runs and `mark_seat_unresolved` (observation.rs ~2021-2085) ends open bindings. workers.rs ~2545 calls `mark_up` for Invalidated. Design lines 706-709 and mod.rs:36/870 say a failed hello "closes nothing"; the native Herdr path returns Err and freezes. Not executed.
  fix-shape hint: return Err (HostUnavailable, with the capture error as cause) from `enumerate_targets` when `capture()` fails, keep CompleteUnverified for the readable-but-unverified case, and add an observe_and_publish test for a refused hc socket.

[Should-fix] src/cli/mod.rs:3940 — The CLI's seat lookup for a lone herdr-core Terminal site is not host-scoped: it queries by bare tN with host None, so two attached cores that both own a seated t1 make every seat-acting CLI command in either terminal fail with 'pane t1 maps to more than one seat', and when only the other core's t1 has a seat the lookup returns that foreign seat. [lanes: correctness]
  verdict: confirmed (reproduce ✓ / refute ✗-survived / ground ✓)
  evidence: run() (mod.rs ~349-357) sets caller_pane to the bare tN; SelfMarker/SeatDefault/derive_caller arms (~3716, ~3741, ~4108) call `located_pane_seat` → `pane_seat` → `pane_seat_on(.., None, ..)` (3883); store/queries.rs:1642 applies the host filter only `if let Some(host)`. `site_capability::seats_host` (site_capability.rs:51) already returns the core socket for a Terminal but only `named_site_seat` (3989) and hook.rs:1583 use it. herdr-core ids are per core and start at t1.
  fix-shape hint: pass `seats_host(site)` into the Terminal path's seat lookup (use `pane_seat_on(.., Some(host), ..)`), and add a two-core CLI caller test.

[lanes: correctness, premortem, simplicity-design]

NotAncestor is cached until the host-set epoch changes. tests/service/locate.rs has no two-core case.
  fix-shape hint: select the host by the candidate's socket via `by_locator` (and carry the socket in the inherited-name hint), falling back to the loop only when no socket is known.

  fix-shape hint: anchor on the harness (the binding's own fingerprint, or the first non-caller process below pane_pid), and add a test where the pane command is the harness itself.
